protocol.description:
With several monitors connected, one of them is usually the main one: where new windows open after monitors were plugged in or out, and where panels and other layer surfaces go that don't ask for an output. This protocol lets an output configuration tool show and choose that primary output.
The compositor remembers the choice for the combination of monitors connected when it is made, and makes the output primary again whenever that combination comes back. Outputs are named as by wl_output.name and zwlr_output_head_v1.name.
Choosing a primary output only says where things go from then on; windows that are open stay where they are.
This is an experimental protocol: backward-incompatible changes may be made, and the interface names carry the "xx" prefix until it is stabilized.

interface.name: xx_primary_output_manager_v1

description.summary: primary output of the connected monitors

interface.description: Right after the global is bound, the compositor sends a primary event with the current primary output, and again whenever it changes, including when monitors come or go.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. The primary output stays as it is.

request.name: set_primary
request.description: Make the named output primary for the monitors connected now, and remember that. The output must be enabled. The compositor answers with a primary event, also when it rejects the request (an unknown or disabled output) or nothing changed, so a client can tell what happened from the next primary event after a roundtrip.

request.name: unset_primary
request.description: Forget the primary output of the monitors connected now. The compositor answers with a primary event.

event.name: primary
event.description: The primary output of the monitors connected now, or null if there is none.
